citations.claim: Initial state: body falling at vy=-60 before integration.
After one step the fall speed grew to ~66 instead of ~61 expected from gravity alone.
First violating step: total energy jumped from 2100 to ~2415 J with zero controller work, exceeding the 2315 J bound.

counterfactual.change: Reduced initial vy from -60 to -5 (single field); slower fall stays within substep regime so no spurious energy gain and no violation.

explanation: Single free-falling body with large dt=1/30 and high speed triggers fast-body substepping (71 substeps reported). Semi-implicit Euler applies gravity each substep while falling, but the effective velocity gain (~6 m/s in 0.033s, i.e. ~180 m/s^2) is ~6x gravity (30). This indicates the substep loop over-integrates gravity / double-counts acceleration for fast bodies, injecting ~315 J in one step with no controller work, breaking energy_bound.
vision_note: The single blue body drops an anomalously large vertical distance between step 0 and step 1. No walls, other bodies, waypoints or collisions are visible to explain such a sudden gain in fall speed.
